references.text: The dream itself that verse 26 interprets: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows and seven lean cows, as well as seven full heads of grain and seven thin heads of grain.
Joseph begins his interpretation by stating that Pharaoh's dream is one—this prepares for the explanation in verse 26 that the seven cows and the seven heads of grain mean the same thing.

Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dream and explains that the seven fat cows and seven good heads of grain represent seven years of abundance, followed by seven years of famine, which directly relates to the meaning of the dream.
The fulfillment of the interpretation: the seven years of abundance in Egypt, where the land produced plentiful crops, just as Joseph predicted.
The fulfillment of Joseph's prophecy about the seven years of famine that followed the seven years of abundance.
Joseph refers to the seven years of famine that had already been going on for two years, confirming his earlier interpretation of Pharaoh's dreams.
Describes how the famine affected the entire region, including Egypt, which aligns with Joseph's interpretation of the seven lean cows and seven thin heads of grain.
Verse 5 shows the actual dream image that verse 26 interprets as seven years of abundance.
Verse 7 illustrates the catastrophic outcome (famine swallows up abundance) that verse 26 explains in terms of timing.
